# LEDGE TO LIFE

## Project
- Subtitle: An intertidal photography story at West Ledge
- Commissioning organisation: coastal learning centre
- Feature title: LEDGE TO LIFE
- Opening line: A shore at three scales
- Scale-bar label: Scale
- Scale structure: shore; microhabitat; organism
- Audience: nature observers; coastal learning centre editorial team
- Session date: 18 September 2026
- Session window: 08:30–09:50 BST
- Low water: 09:10 BST; 0.8 m above chart datum

## Site
- Study area: West Ledge
- East–west extent: 20000 mm
- North–south extent: 12000 mm
- Coordinate origin: southwest corner
- Positive x: east
- Positive y: north
- Landward side: north
- Seaward side: south
- S1: x 6000 mm; y 4000 mm; exposed rock ledge; specimen L1
- S2: x 14000 mm; y 6000 mm; shallow pool margin; specimen P1
- Pool bounds: x 12000–16000 mm; y 6000–9000 mm

## Subjects
| Specimen | Sample | Common name | Scientific name | Measurement | Appearance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | S1 | Common limpet | Patella vulgata | Shell length 32 mm | Grey-white conical shell; radiating ribs; apex slightly forward of centre |
| P1 | S2 | Common periwinkle | Littorina littorea | Shell height 18 mm | Dark grey-brown pointed shell; six whorls; lighter apex; dark spiral lines |

## Photography and layout
- Light: diffuse ambient daylight
- Starting aperture: f/8
- Starting shutter speed: 1/250 s
- Ruler: matte white; 50 mm measuring span; 1 mm graduations; numbered every 10 mm
- Whole-organism scale bars: 5 mm
- Shell-detail scale bars: 1 mm
- Outer inset: 5% of frame width and height
- Caption zone: bottom 15% of frame height
- Observation video duration: 10 seconds

## Species reference sources
- Common limpet morphology: [MarLIN — Common limpet](https://www.marlin.ac.uk/species/detail/1371)
- Common periwinkle morphology: [MarLIN — Common periwinkle](https://www.marlin.ac.uk/species/detail/1328)

steps.userMessage:
LEDGE TO LIFE | An intertidal photography story at West Ledge

We are commissioning a photographic observation feature for visitors to our coastal learning centre. The title is "LEDGE TO LIFE" and the opening line is "A shore at three scales". Work within the West Ledge study area, 20000 mm east–west by 12000 mm north–south, during the session on 18 September 2026, 08:30–09:50 BST. Low water is at 09:10 BST, 0.8 m above chart datum. The story moves from the shore to two microhabitats and then to the shells within them.

Our two subjects are L1, a Common limpet, Patella vulgata, with a 32 mm shell at S1, and P1, a Common periwinkle, Littorina littorea, with an 18 mm shell height at S2. L1 has a grey-white conical shell with radiating ribs; P1 has a dark grey-brown pointed shell with six whorls and a lighter apex. Their appearance and sample locations carry through the series. Photograph both in their existing positions using diffuse ambient daylight, with an initial setting of f/8 and 1/250 s. Camera position and composition are yours to develop. Captions describe the visible shell, substrate and water conditions alongside the supplied records.

Audience: nature observers and the coastal learning centre's editorial team, choosing an observation feature that helps visitors relate small organisms to their surroundings.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the project facts and fixed wording. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md contains the proportions, formats and stages for all 14 files. 03-site-records.en.md contains the study boundary, sample coordinates and tide context. 04-observation-records.en.md contains the specimen names, measurements and visible characteristics. west-ledge-plan.png locates both samples within the study area and marks the session window. caption-crop-geometry.png defines the image inset and caption zone across three proportions. limpet-identity.png records L1's shell appearance. periwinkle-identity.png records P1's shell appearance. field-ruler.png records the 50 mm measuring ruler and its graduations. coastal-light-reference.png provides empty-shore daylight and wet-rock atmosphere.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page photographic concept and lighting specification, with the three-scale structure, eight shot IDs W1, W2, M1, M2, O1, O2, D1 and D2, sample assignments, proposed viewpoints, daylight approach, starting camera settings, session window and low-water record
2. Two shore photographs, W1 establishing West Ledge and W2 locating S1 and S2 within the same shore
3. Two microhabitat photographs, M1 showing L1 on the exposed ledge at S1 and M2 showing P1 at the shallow pool margin at S2
4. Two whole-organism photographs, O1 of L1 and O2 of P1, each with a calibrated 5 mm scale bar
5. Two shell-detail photographs, D1 of L1's radiating ribs and D2 of P1's spiral surface, each with a calibrated 1 mm scale bar
6. Two additional crops of O1, one square and one portrait, retaining the complete shell, scale bar and caption
7. One caption and sequence document containing eight numbered photographs, their shot IDs, specimen and sample IDs, common and scientific names, measurements, capture times, tide context and recorded camera settings
8. One 10-second observation video moving through W1, M1, O1, M2 and O2, with the project title, opening line and low-water time
9. One observation presentation of at least eight pages, reusing the specification, eight photographs, two crops, caption sequence and video storyboard

Acceptance:
- The photographic specification assigns all eight shot IDs to the three scales. The caption and sequence document and presentation repeat its 08:30–09:50 BST window, 09:10 BST low water at 0.8 m, and diffuse ambient daylight approach; their photograph entries retain the same shot IDs and sample assignments.
- W1 and W2 establish the mapped West Ledge area and its two samples. M1, O1 and D1 retain L1 at S1 with its 32 mm grey-white ribbed shell; M2, O2 and D2 retain P1 at S2 with its 18 mm dark grey-brown shell, six whorls and lighter apex, matching the two identity references.
- O1 and O2 carry 5 mm bars and D1 and D2 carry 1 mm bars, each labelled "Scale" and calibrated from the field ruler recorded in the relevant subject plane. Their captions and the caption document distinguish L1's shell length from P1's shell height.
- The square and portrait O1 crops retain the same shell and a scale bar recalculated for each crop. All ten photographic layouts use the bottom 15% caption zone and a 5% outer inset; the whole shells in O1, O2 and both O1 crops sit within that inset.
- The caption and sequence document orders the eight photographs W1, W2, M1, O1, D1, M2, O2, D2. Its captions pair S1 with L1 and S2 with P1, use Patella vulgata and Littorina littorea as recorded, and describe visible shell, substrate and water conditions with capture times inside the session window.
- The 10-second video follows W1, M1, O1, M2, O2. Its opening and the presentation's first page print LEDGE TO LIFE and A shore at three scales. The presentation has at least eight pages, reuses all eight photographs and both crops, and identifies the pages containing the specification facts, caption sequence and video storyboard.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
